title: Dilution-fridge-grade helium recapture ring on every etch chuck
idea: Quantum-computing labs recover >95% of helium boil-off; copy them by adding an edge-scavenging vacuum ring around each electrostatic chuck that captures backside-cooling helium leakage and feeds a tool-side membrane purifier and compressor returning 99.999% He to the chuck line. A fab helium 'bank' meters per-tool recovery the way a cryo lab does.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30% offline since March 2026): cuts fab He purchases ~80-90% with small capex and protects etch/CVD uptime.

title: Rocket-test-stand hydrogen as backside wafer coolant instead of helium
idea: Rocket engine test stands handle hydrogen routinely, and H2 conducts heat better than He (0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K). Run chuck backside cooling on 5-20 Torr electrolytic H2 (or H2/Ar) with leak-tight seals, H2 sensors and dilution exhaust, qualifying each etch chemistry for H-radical side effects.
why: Removes the largest fab helium use in etch and deposition; H2 is made domestically on site from water and power, with equal or better wafer temperature control.

title: Fiber-optic preform silica lines CZ crucibles, ending Spruce Pine dependence
idea: Optical-fiber makers need ppb-pure silica and synthesize it by flame hydrolysis of SiCl4 instead of mining it. Polysilicon plants produce SiCl4 as a byproduct: turn it into synthetic silica soot and sinter a 3-5 mm bubble-free inner liner onto a crucible shell made from ordinary non-Spruce quartz sand.
why: HPQ crucibles are >80% Spruce Pine: a synthetic inner layer could cut HPQ per crucible ~70% and turns a polysilicon waste stream into a strategic input.

title: Containerless space-furnace logic: cold-crucible induction Czochralski for 300 mm
idea: Space crystal growers avoid containers altogether. On Earth, a segmented water-cooled copper cold crucible with induction heating makes silicon hold itself inside a frozen Si skull, so the melt never touches quartz. Controlled O2/Ar ambient or SiO dosing restores the oxygen needed for intrinsic gettering, and cusp magnetic fields steady the melt.
why: Eliminates quartz crucibles entirely (the HPQ chokepoint) and lowers metal contamination, at roughly 2x melt power, which is small next to crucible scarcity risk.

title: Solar-megafab continuous Czochralski: five ingots per crucible for DRAM wafers
idea: Solar ingot pullers run continuous CZ, recharging granular polysilicon while pulling, so one crucible yields 5-8 ingots instead of one. Port CCZ with fluidized-bed granular feeders and in-situ melt-level control to 300 mm prime DRAM-grade ingots, using oxygen-transport models to keep interstitial oxygen uniform over the long campaign.
why: Cuts HPQ crucibles per wafer ~5x and puller energy per kg ~20-30%, directly offsetting the Spruce Pine risk.

title: Hurricane-proof quartz: chlorination-upgraded vein quartz from five countries
idea: Hurricane Helene's 2024 shutdown of Spruce Pine is the extreme edge case: design crucible supply to survive it. Upgrade ordinary hydrothermal vein and pegmatite quartz (Norway, Brazil, India, Quebec, Arizona) by 1200 C Cl2/HCl gas leaching plus electrodiffusion 'sweeping', the field-driven alkali removal used for oscillator-grade quartz, to reach <10 ppm total impurities.
why: Second-sources the >80% single-region HPQ chokepoint through geographic diversity instead of reliance on one ore body.

title: HBM stacks peel off backside silicon instead of grinding it away
idea: HBM dies are thinned from 775 um to ~30-50 um, which grinds ~95% of every wafer into sludge. A laser-written subsurface damage plane plus polymer-stress cold split, as already used on SiC boules, cleaves off a ~700 um slab that is repolished and reused as monitor, test or epi-base wafers.
why: Recovers ~0.9 wafer of silicon per HBM wafer for the fastest-growing DRAM segment, cutting polysilicon, HPQ crucible demand, grinding water and slurry.

title: Kerfless solar trick: epi DRAM wafers lifted off reusable porous-silicon parents
idea: Kerfless solar firms grow epitaxial wafers on porous-silicon release layers and reuse the parent wafer dozens of times. For DRAM, grow a 20-50 um device-grade epi layer on double-porous Si, bond it to a cheap carrier (UMG or recycled Si), split it off, and repolish the CZ parent for 10-20 reuses.
why: Only the top few um of a DRAM wafer are active: cuts prime CZ silicon, HPQ crucibles and polysilicon per bit ~10x.

title: Trusted-foundry molybdenum wordlines from Colorado ore replace Chinese tungsten
idea: Defense trusted-foundry users must avoid adversary-sourced metals. Molybdenum is mined in the U.S. (Climax, Henderson) and has a shorter electron mean free path than W, so it beats W resistivity in <20 nm trenches. Deposit Mo by ALD/CVD from MoO2Cl2 into buried wordlines and bit-line contacts with thin or no TiN liner.
why: Removes ~80%-China tungsten and WF6 from the cell array and lowers wordline RC ~20-30% thanks to liner-less fill.

title: Tailings-reprocessing mindset: cold-trap and refluorinate escaped WF6
idea: Miners now reprocess old tailings for the metal left in them, and CVD-W tools likewise send most of their WF6 to the exhaust. Put a cryogenic/sorbent trap ahead of abatement to catch WF6 and WOxFy, then refluorinate the captured material with on-site F2 back into WF6 feedstock.
why: Raises tungsten utilization from ~20-30% to >70%, cutting W import need per wafer ~2-3x while W is still in the process.

title: Jeweler's bench-sweep recovery for sputter targets and chamber shields
idea: Jewelers recover gold dust from bench sweeps, while fabs scrap sputter targets at ~30-40% utilization and bead-blast metal off chamber shields into waste. Move to rotating cylindrical targets (>80% utilization) and send shield and target residues to closed-loop hydrometallurgy that recovers Ti, Ta, Co and W, with chain of custody back to the target makers.
why: Cuts virgin tantalum (conflict mineral), tungsten and cobalt per wafer ~2x.

title: Uranium-enrichment fluorine plants: on-site F2 replaces NF3 and fluorocarbons
idea: Uranium enrichment has made elemental fluorine electrolytically at ton scale for 80 years. Put modular KF-2HF electrolyzers at each fab: F2 replaces NF3 (GWP ~17,000) for chamber cleans and serves as a carbon-free fluorine-radical source, fed by HF recovered from fab fluoride wastewater.
why: Cuts PFC/PFAS-class gas use and GHG emissions; recycling wastewater HF eases fluorspar dependence (China ~60%).

title: Space-station water loop: 98% UPW recovery with vapor-compression distillation
idea: The ISS recycles ~98% of its water with vapor-compression distillation and catalytic oxidation. Build fab reclaim the same way: segregate rinse streams by contamination class, send low-TOC rinses straight back through UV/RO/EDI, and push high-TOC streams through mechanical-vapor-recompression distillation, targeting 90-98% reuse.
why: Water limits Arizona and Texas fabs: cuts withdrawal ~5-10x and opens water-scarce U.S. regions for siting.

title: Bitcoin-miner siting: DRAM fabs at stranded hydro and flare gas
idea: Crypto miners chase stranded megawatts in Pacific Northwest hydro, Texas flare gas and curtailed wind. Site new U.S. DRAM capacity at those nodes with interruptible-load contracts covering deferrable loads (abatement, UPW heating, test and burn-in) and cold-climate free cooling for chillers.
why: Energy is a growing share of wafer cost under EUV: buying at <$30/MWh and skipping grid-queue delays could halve power cost and shorten time to power.

title: Satellite-lidar solid-state 193 nm source frees lithography from neon
idea: Spaceborne UV instruments cannot carry gas bottles, so they use frequency-multiplied solid-state lasers. Build a 193 nm source from a high-power Yb fiber laser and an OPO mixed through a CLBO sum-frequency cascade, sized for non-critical ArF-dry and periphery layers.
why: Excimer lasers depend on neon and krypton, historically ~50% from Ukraine/Russia: this removes rare-gas consumption and laser-gas refill downtime.

title: Xenon-anesthesia recapture logic for every rare gas in fab exhaust
idea: Hospitals recapture exhaled xenon anesthetic with cryogenic adsorbers because Xe is so scarce, yet fabs dump Ne, Kr and Xe from lasers, implanters and etchers. Fit point-of-use pressure-swing/cryo-adsorption cartridges that capture rare gases before dilution and regenerate them centrally to 99.99%.
why: Cuts neon, krypton and xenon purchases ~70-90%, defusing a war-exposed chokepoint.

title: Hyperscale DIMM harvest: retired DDR4 dies reborn as CXL memory
idea: Industrial users with 30-year lines already buy reclaimed chips, and hyperscalers retire millions of DDR4 DIMMs every 4-5 years. An automated U.S. harvesting line tests retired DIMMs, bins them by retention and refresh margin, and mounts them behind CXL memory-expander controllers as a cheap far-memory tier.
why: Zero new wafers or chokepoint materials: ~10-20% of server DRAM demand could come from the installed base at a fraction of the cost per bit.

title: Wartime materials board: per-gigabyte chokepoint-intensity procurement standard
idea: WWII production boards rationed tin and rubber by making designers report and cap use per unit. Require a certified 'chokepoint ledger' per gigabyte (mg W, liters He, g HPQ, g PFAS, liters UPW) for CHIPS-funded and DoD purchases, with price preferences for parts under a declining cap, like CAFE standards for memory.
why: Creates market pull for every substitution idea; targets a 50% cut in chokepoint intensity per GB in 5 years.

title: Training activation-stash memory: 100 ms retention, no high-k capacitor
idea: AI training stashes activations for only ~10-500 ms between forward and backward passes, an extreme user that never needs 64 ms-class retention. Build a dedicated stash DRAM with planar or shallow-trench SiO2/SiN capacitors (~0.5 fF) sized so data turnover beats worst-case retention, plus a deadline-tracking controller that refreshes only pages older than their budget.
why: Drops ZrO2/HfO2 ALD, TiN pillars and 60-75:1 fluorocarbon etch from the array (facts 1, 3), cutting capacitor-module materials and steps ~40%.

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory pods: cold kills leakage, so capacitors shrink
idea: Cryo-CMOS users at 77 K see junction and subthreshold leakage fall by 6+ orders of magnitude, so a few tenths of a fF holds charge for hours. Immerse memory sleds in LN2 made from air on site (not helium), with tiny planar or capacitorless floating-body cells, and recover cold through the data center's air-separation unit.
why: Removes high-k capacitor materials and high-AR etch, and makes refresh energy (fact 3) near zero; wire resistance also drops, partly offsetting the cooling penalty.

title: Astronomy CCD shift-register memory for streaming KV-cache reads
idea: Astronomers' CCDs move charge packets with >99.9999% transfer efficiency using only polysilicon gates over oxide, with no per-cell contacts or metal capacitors. KV-cache reads are long sequential streams, so build CCD loop memories with sense amps every few thousand stages, ~4F2 cells, and refresh by circulation.
why: Eliminates per-cell W contacts and high-k capacitor stacks and shrinks periphery (fact 7); materials and cost per bit may be ~2-3x lower for streaming tiers.

title: Venus-lander silicon carbide gain cell: retention measured in years
idea: NASA's SiC JFET ICs have run for a year at 460 C in Venus conditions, and at room temperature the same 3.3 eV bandgap makes storage-node leakage ~1e-21 A. Build a 2T SiC gain cell that stores charge on a JFET gate junction, so memory needs no refresh, no capacitor dielectric and no tungsten.
why: Removes refresh (fact 3) and hafnia/zirconia capacitors; serves 200 C industrial, automotive and space tiers now, and gets cheaper as EV demand drives SiC wafer costs down.

title: Constellation-satellite short-life qualification trims barrier and liner metals
idea: Satellite constellations fly parts qualified for 5 years, not 25, and AI-accelerator DRAM is scrapped after ~4 years. Define an 'AI-life' DRAM grade with 4-year electromigration and TDDB targets that allows thinner TaN/TiN barriers and liners, Al instead of W in periphery local interconnect, and reduced reliability guardbands.
why: Cuts Ta, Ti and W per wafer ~30-50% and removes some process steps.

title: Lunar-base abundant-element PDK: a gain cell from only eight elements
idea: A Moon-base fab could use only regolith-abundant elements, so impose that rule in a university nanofab: build a 2T gain-cell array from Si, O, N, Al, Ti and H (plus B/P dopants) only, with poly-Si channels, LPCVD SiO2/Si3N4, ALD Al2O3, sputtered Al and TiN, and contact lithography on 100 mm wafers. Benchmark retention against a W/ZrO2 reference.
why: Proves a chokepoint-free memory process (no W, Hf, Zr, Ta, Co, In or Ga) and gives a template for a resource-proof U.S. DRAM tier.

title: $1-IoT zinc-tin-oxide gain cells, indium and gallium free
idea: Disposable $1 IoT tags push oxide transistors toward the cheapest metals. Sputter amorphous Zn-Sn-O (ZTO) as the channel of 2T0C gain cells with ALD Al2O3 gate dielectric and Al or Mo electrodes, annealed below 350 C in a university fab.
why: IGZO gain cells (prior work) depend on indium (China ~60%) and export-controlled gallium; ZTO uses abundant Zn and Sn while aiming for the ~1e-19 A off-current needed for long retention (fact 3).

title: Naval-reactor hafnium trap avoided: zirconia-only periphery gate stacks
idea: Hafnium exists only as a byproduct of making Hf-free zirconium for naval and power reactors, so its supply is hostage to nuclear demand. Build DRAM-periphery HKMG transistors with ALD ZrO2 or La-doped ZrO2 on a SiON interlayer (TEMAZ precursor, standard in university ALD) and characterize EOT, mobility and PBTI against HfO2.
why: Removes hafnium from DRAM periphery using zirconium, which is roughly 20-50x more available, at similar k ~25-35.

title: MLCC-style strontium titanate nanolaminate stretches pillar capacitors past k=70
idea: MLCC makers ship trillions of titanate capacitors made from abundant Ba, Sr and Ti. Grow ALD SrTiO3/TiO2 nanolaminates (Sr cyclopentadienyl + TTIP, two-step crystallization) inside TiN-lined pillars in a university fab, with Al2O3 interface doping to tame leakage.
why: Fact 1 says k ~70 is needed; STO reaches k ~100-150 below 10 nm, enabling ~2x Cs or ~40% shorter pillars (less high-AR etch and PFC gas).

title: Dental-resin chemistry for fluorine-free photoacid generators
idea: Dental composites are cured in human mouths with non-fluorinated photoinitiators because PFAS is unacceptable there. Synthesize non-fluorinated PAGs (sulfonium salts of camphorsulfonate or bulky sulfonated aromatic anions that limit acid diffusion) and benchmark sensitivity, LER and diffusion length on i-line and e-beam in a university fab.
why: The EU universal PFAS restriction threatens PFBS/PFOS-type PAGs in DRAM resists; a drop-in non-PFAS chemistry keeps the lithography supply legal and secure.

title: Satellite-optics CO2-snow and supercritical CO2 cleaning replaces RCA rinses
idea: Spacecraft optics are cleaned with CO2 snow jets because liquids leave residues in vacuum. In a university fab, replace selected post-etch and pre-deposition SC1/SC2 cleans with CO2-snow particle removal and supercritical CO2 with co-solvent for residue strip, measuring particle adders and metals by TXRF.
why: Each RCA clean uses tens of liters of UPW plus acids; CO2 is a recycled industrial byproduct; target ~30% fewer wet steps and UPW use.

title: Radiation-detector diamond: carbon access transistors with near-zero leakage
idea: Particle-physics and implant users rely on CVD diamond because its 5.5 eV bandgap gives essentially no leakage. Build hydrogen-terminated diamond surface-channel FETs with ALD Al2O3 passivation as DRAM access devices, on polycrystalline diamond grown in a university microwave-plasma CVD reactor.
why: Carbon from methane is unlimited; diamond access devices could cut the 13 fA leakage tail (fact 3) by >1000x and end refresh. Mobility, stability and integration are high risk.

title: Transient-implant chemistry: cleavable-crosslink underfill frees good dies from bad stacks
idea: Biodegradable implant electronics are designed to come apart on cue. Formulate stack underfill and mold compound with acid-cleavable acetal/ketal crosslinks that survive reflow but dissolve in a mild acid bath, so a stack with one bad die is taken apart and its good dies are re-stacked. Test bond strength, warpage and debond in a university packaging lab.
why: HBM stack yield loss (fact 6: 20-30%) throws away fully processed good dies; reclaiming them cuts wafer starts and all materials per good stack ~10-20%.

title: HVAC-technician tracer gas: hydrogen/nitrogen leak checks replace helium
idea: HVAC and automotive leak technicians use 5% H2 in N2 with palladium sniffers because it is cheap and needs no helium. Requalify vacuum-tool leak checking in a university fab using forming-gas tracer, H2-selective sensors and an RGA tuned to mass 2, and document a minimum detectable leak of ~1e-7 mbar-L/s.
why: Removes a recurring helium use at near-zero cost while supply is disrupted, with a procedure fabs can copy.

title: Cryogenic-etch silicon mold builds capacitor holes without fluorocarbon gases
idea: Extreme-cold etching (-110 C SF6/O2 DRIE) carves 50:1+ holes in silicon behind an SiOxFy passivation that evaporates on warm-up, with no C4F6/C4F8 polymer. Replace the oxide capacitor mold with amorphous Si, etch the holes cryogenically in a university ICP tool, deposit TiN/ZrO2/TiN, then strip the Si mold with XeF2 vapor behind a SiN support lattice.
why: Removes PFAS-class, high-GWP fluorocarbon gases from DRAM's highest-AR step (fact 1) and uses faster, cheaper Si etching.

title: Swimming-pool ozone chemistry replaces sulfuric-peroxide resist strip
idea: Pools and bottling plants sanitize with dissolved ozone instead of harsh chemicals. Strip photoresist and organics with high-concentration ozonated UPW (>80 ppm, with UV assist and CO2 spiking to protect surfaces) in a university wet bench, benchmarking against SPM on implanted resist.
why: SPM consumes large volumes of sulfuric acid, peroxide and rinse water; ozone is made from oxygen on demand, cutting chemical purchases and wastewater ~80%.

title: Space-shower mist rinse: megasonic aerosol rinses with one-tenth the water
idea: Astronauts wash with mist and no-rinse methods because water is precious. Replace overflow-bath rinses with megasonic-atomized UPW mist and an in-line resistivity endpoint that stops rinsing when the drain returns to 18 MOhm-cm, prototyped on a university spin-rinse-dryer.
why: Rinsing is most of a fab's UPW use; endpoint-controlled mist rinsing could cut rinse water ~70-90%.

title: Downhole-tool silicide: fully silicided titanium buried wordlines without tungsten
idea: 200 C downhole electronics favor refractory silicides that stay stable when hot. Fill the recessed gate trench with doped poly-Si and convert it fully to C54 TiSi2 (or NiSi) by RTA, with the TiN barrier doubling as work-function metal, all with university-fab sputter and RTA tools.
why: Removes W and WF6 from buried wordlines using abundant Ti and Si; fully silicided lines reach ~15-20 uOhm-cm, competitive with W in narrow trenches.

title: Aircraft anodizing tank grows billions of capacitor molds without lithography
idea: Aerospace anodizing self-organizes aluminum into hexagonal nanopore arrays with AR >1000:1 using only Al, acid and volts. Sputter Al on the wafer, nanoimprint a pre-texture that registers pores to the access-transistor grid, two-step anodize to 40-60 nm pitch, then ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN inside the pores.
why: Replaces EUV hole patterning and fluorocarbon high-AR plasma etch (facts 1, 4); AR 100:1+ pushes Cs well past today's ~5 fF wall.

title: Black-silicon solar etch: catalyst-guided holes reach 100:1 without plasma
idea: Black-silicon solar texturing uses metal-assisted chemical etching (MACE): a patterned Ag film sinks into Si in HF/H2O2 and drills straight holes. Pattern a catalyst mesh by e-beam or nanoimprint in a university fab to drill registered 100:1+ trenches for capacitors or vertical channels, then remove the catalyst with iodide etch plus sacrificial oxidation and verify retention.
why: Plasma-free high-AR etch removes fluorocarbon gases, etch-tool capital and chamber parts and reaches the AR ~115 that fact 1 calls for; metal contamination is the key risk.

title: Printed-electronics aqueous cluster inks replace organometallic ALD precursors
idea: Roll-to-roll printed-electronics makers spin aqueous inorganic clusters (Al13 hydroxo clusters, zirconium oxo-nitrate clusters) that densify into dense oxide films at ~300 C. Spin-coat AlOx/ZrOx dielectrics from water-based inks in a university fab and compare leakage, k and step coverage with ALD.
why: Removes costly, supply-concentrated organometallic precursors and vacuum tools from some dielectric layers; material use ~90% versus ~10-30% for ALD.

title: Film-capacitor self-healing: clearing electrodes rescue thin high-k capacitors
idea: Industrial power film capacitors last 30 years because a thin metallization vaporizes around any breakdown spot and isolates it. Build MIM capacitor arrays with a 3-5 nm Al or Ti top-electrode skin that burns back locally under a forming pulse, healing weak spots before a TiN cap goes on, and measure yield versus dielectric thickness in a university fab.
why: Lets ZrO2 stacks thin ~20-30% (higher Cs or shorter pillars) without leakage-tail failures, meaning fewer Zr precursors and less high-AR etch per bit.

title: PCB plating-shop logic: electroless nickel-boron plugs replace tungsten contacts
idea: Circuit-board makers fill microvias with electroless metal, with no vacuum and no fluoride gases. Fill bit-line and periphery contacts bottom-up with electroless Ni-B on a NiSi seed that catalyzes deposition without scarce palladium, using suppressor additives for void-free superfill on a university plating bench.
why: Removes WF6 and tungsten (~80% China) from contacts and avoids CVD tool capex; Ni-B resistivity is higher than W but acceptable for short plugs.

title: Photonic curing: flash-lamp crystallizes zirconia in milliseconds, not furnace hours
idea: Plastic-substrate electronics that cannot exceed 150 C are cured with millisecond xenon flash lamps. Use flash-lamp annealing to crystallize ZrO2 into its high-k tetragonal phase and activate dopants in milliseconds instead of furnace anneals, tested on a university flash/RTA tool.
why: Furnaces are big energy and thermal-budget sinks: ms anneals cut anneal energy ~10x and can raise tetragonal fraction (higher k, more Cs).

title: Low-budget-fab block copolymers print the honeycomb capacitor array without EUV
idea: Fabs that cannot buy EUV (universities, developing nations) can use directed self-assembly. High-chi block-copolymer cylinders (PS-b-P2VP) guided by a sparse e-beam or i-line template, hardened by sequential infiltration synthesis of AlOx, print the hexagonal capacitor array at ~30 nm pitch.
why: Replaces one of DRAM's 5-7 EUV layers (fact 4) with spin-coat and bake, cutting dependence on the single EUV supplier for that layer.

title: Solar PERC spatial ALD: atmospheric-pressure dielectrics at 10x throughput
idea: Solar lines deposit Al2O3 passivation by spatial ALD, moving wafers under separated precursor zones at atmospheric pressure. Build a bench spatial-ALD head in a university fab for ZrO2/Al2O3 capacitor and liner films, and measure precursor utilization and conformality in 10:1 trenches.
why: Conventional ALD wastes most of its precursor and needs vacuum; spatial ALD could cut Zr/Hf organometallic use, pump energy and tool capital per wafer ~2-5x.

title: MEMS-release vapor HF replaces wet buffered-oxide etch and rinses
idea: MEMS makers release structures with anhydrous vapor HF and an alcohol catalyst, using no liquids. Replace wet BOE/DHF oxide strips with vapor HF in a university fab, recovering HF in a closed cylinder loop, and quantify selectivity to nitride and residues.
why: Cuts HF wastewater, rinse UPW and fluoride sludge per wafer, which matters most at water-scarce U.S. sites.

title: Spacecraft thermal straps: gasless nanotube chucks remove helium backside cooling
idea: Spacecraft move heat across vacuum joints with compliant metallic and CNT interfaces. Grow a vertically aligned CNT or Cu-nanowire forest on the chuck surface (university CVD or electroplating) so electrostatic clamping alone gives >2000 W/m2-K contact conductance without backside gas, and test particle shedding.
why: Removes helium from etch and deposition chucks entirely (Qatar risk) and simplifies chuck gas hardware.
